Washington created the affordability crisis – now politicians are scrambling for solutions to win back voters. Most of them won't work. Cato’s Handbook on Affordability offers a more honest and responsible approach that addresses the root causes of America's cost of living woes.

Video

The traditional view blamed oil price spikes on supply disruptions from wars or OPEC decisions. But newer research shows most major swings since 1973 are largely driven by changes in global demand.  

But the current shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz reduces world supply by about 20 percent, almost 8 times larger than we experienced in 1980, Cato’s Peter Van Doren writes.
ow.ly/qUU250YEAkb

Many people think Canada has government-run health care while the US has a free-market system. In reality, both are government-run—they’re just structured differently. Cato’s @dr4liberty explains.
ow.ly/8jHQ50YEvzA

A more stable measure of US economic growth – real final sales to domestic purchasers – decelerated in 2025, even with a big AI tailwind. Trade policy might not have caused this slowdown, but it’s clear that tariffs didn’t create “the strongest economy in history,” Cato scholars explain. 

ow.ly/Ncvv50YEw8g

Free expression is now met with growing suspicion across the globe. In “The Future of Free Speech,” @JMchangama and Jeff Kosseff discuss how we got here. Join us for a conversation on how free speech can meet modern challenges without abandoning its foundational role. 
  
Register: ow.ly/FZjT50YEBs2

Vast energy resources. Abundant water supply. Cool temperatures. @RepNickBegich argues Alaska could be a hub for the data center buildout AI demands. Cato's @KevinTFrazier presses him on local opposition—and gets an answer rooted in Alaska's unique resource governance. 

ow.ly/koPw50YEuqa

Steve Davies’s “The Great Realignment” argues politics is shifting from markets vs. state control to nationalism and sovereignty vs. cosmopolitanism and globalism. In a new Cato Podcast, @MrRBourne talks with @SteveDavies365 about why today’s key battles center on borders, culture, and who governs—and what that means for libertarians and economic policy.

Apple: ow.ly/TrCj50YE5wC  
Spotify: ow.ly/7yJK50YE5wE  
Our website: ow.ly/UXZj50YE5wI

Raising the FDIC cap is a solution in search of a problem. Fewer than 1% of accounts exceed $250K, and those who do already have workarounds. Expanding the cap won’t help Main Street—it just grows government’s role in banking. Let it die, says Cato’s @norbertjmichel. 
ow.ly/hyz050YEzNz

Sammy's Law mandates new API rules for third-party safety tools. It’s a workable solution. But 30-day implementation timelines, vague and invasive disclosure rules, and costly compliance mandates could kill the market before it starts. Cato's Christopher Gardner and @dr_inserra explain.
ow.ly/LLOr50YEvhB

America has gone more than a year without a surgeon general—and most people haven’t noticed. That’s because the job is largely symbolic, while real public health work happens elsewhere. 

Instead of rushing to fill it, Congress should consider eliminating it altogether, writes Cato's @dr4liberty.
ow.ly/s4Ti50YEtxM

The Trump administration’s use of extrajudicial violence—such as bombing boats and shooting protesters—undermines the rule of law. When agents act with impunity, accountability erodes, democratic norms weaken, and the US risks becoming a global pariah, warns Cato’s Walter Olson. 
ow.ly/nOlB50YEvnL

Argentina was once a top 10 world economy under classical liberal policies. Cato’s @hiperfalcon argues that Peronism—a form of fascism—stopped that prosperity, and its 80-year persistence explains why Argentina's decline was unlike any other nation’s.

ow.ly/YZNv50YE0us

Not only has the Jones Act failed to ensure a robust commercial shipbuilding industry, but it also often means that needed ships don’t exist at all. 

New England can’t buy LNG from the rest of the US because there are no ships that comply with the 1920 law to transport it, reports Cato’s @cpgrabow, who was interviewed on CBS’s “60 Minutes” about the topic. 
ow.ly/4cCO50YEyNN

Viktor Orbán’s Hungary shows what happens when governments bypass checks and balances, says @johanknorberg. 

Learn how removing constraints on government power can unleash corruption, cronyism, and rent-seeking: ow.ly/7C1350YE169

Video

Who owns your digital data—you or Big Tech? 

In Chatrie v. U.S., the Court should make clear: your emails, location history, and search data can be your “papers,” even when stored by companies. The Fourth Amendment shouldn’t vanish in the cloud, argue @bskorup and Laura Bondank. 
ow.ly/4ZRT50YEuUv

The One Big Beautiful Bill limits gambling loss deductions to 90%, taxing income gamblers never earned. It's a small change with big implications—the tax code systematically penalizes risk-taking by capping losses across gambling, business, and investment, explains Cato's @adamnmichel.

ow.ly/xyFv50YCYQy

The United States has not negotiated any free trade agreements since 2020. Meanwhile, other countries—including some of America’s largest trading partners and long-standing allies—have continued to negotiate and enter into numerous such deals, according to Cato scholars. 

ow.ly/EMCM50YCvSy

The Durbin Amendment capped debit swipe fees. Banks raised minimum balances and other fees, and cut other services. Many retailers raised their prices. Low-income consumers were hit hardest. Now Congress wants to do it again—for credit cards. Cato's @SolveigSinglet and Ryan Chan-Wei say the market has a better answer.

ow.ly/LYQN50YCVMp
